newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland steps up NATO plans, even as Russia objects.
newsitem.headline: Poland steps up NATO plans, even as Russia objects.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Tuesday that even as Russian leaders stepped up opposition to NATO enlargement, Warsaw was forging ahead with its own preparations to join the Western alliance.

Cimoszewicz was asked by a radio interviewer to comment on a Monday meeting in Moscow, at which President Boris Yeltsin and other Russian chiefs confirmed their objections to NATO's eastward expansion and decided to draw up a plan of action.

He replied that also on Monday Poland's National Defence Committee (KOK), grouping its president, prime minister, key ministers, parliamentary and army leaders, had met and set up a special body to harmonise their actions concerning NATO.

"We decided to call a special team of the KOK responsible for coordinating our preparations for NATO membership," Cimoszewicz told public radio, adding that the body would be headed by Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati.
Cimoszewicz said it was coincidence the Moscow and Warsaw meetings had happened at around the same time.

"But both events only signal something that should not be a secret for anyone -- the continued difference of opinion between Russia on the one hand and the NATO member states and countries like Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary which are interested in NATO membership on the other," he said.

The three former Soviet satellites are expected to be the first to get membership invitations from NATO in July, despite Russia's view that this will threaten its security, and Poland is intensifying practical preparations for entry talks.
Diplomats say Moscow is chiefly concerned over the entry of Poland, a large country bordering Russia's Kaliningrad region.
Yeltsin aide Sergei Shakhrai on Monday said Russia's most effective response to NATO enlargement would be to forge ahead with a union with Belarus, which borders on Poland.
Cimoszewicz said Russia and Belarus were anyway drawing closer.
"I think this process is continuing independently of what is happening in and around NATO and I would not link the issues," Cimoszewicz said.
